pairs.why: A keeps an even bright magenta field with gentle ring steps like the real card, while B darkens the corners into a heavier vignette.
B has the lighter, warmer overall key with a pale yellow wall and a mid-value floor, while A's dark grey floor adds a heavy dark mass the real bright cards lack.
A's local contrast inside the hero is softer, like the real cards, but its pale silver top has weak value separation from the yellow, so B is not clearly worse.
B has a bright glow right behind the bottle with darker orange corners, which matches the real card's burst, and its bottle is a more saturated mid value.
A has the soft drop shadow and mid-value green field with gentle gradients, while B has a hard flat ground band and a hard ellipse shadow.
Both have nearly the same key, value groups and shadow placement, so value gives no reason to choose.
Both have a bright cyan upper left falling to dark blue with a dark navy hero, and neither is clearly closer to the real card's darker, calmer field.
B's pale tile floor and lighter water give a higher key with a softer hero-to-ground relationship, closer to the real card's bright floor.
